newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor turns up heat in diplomat spat.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor turns up heat in diplomat spat.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani stepped up his campaign on Monday against two diplomats from Russia and Belarus involved in a fight with police, demanding Belarus pay more than $41,000 in outstanding traffic tickets.
The mayor also accused the ambassador of Belarus of concocting "a pack of lies" in an account of the December 29 incident the ambassador submitted to the U.S. State Department.

Police said two officers pulled the Russian diplomat from his car because he appeared intoxicated after parking illegally near a fire hydrant. They said the Belarus diplomat then punched one of the police officers.
The charges against the envoys, both attached to U.N. missions, were dropped after they claimed diplomatic immunity.

But according to a letter written by Ambassador Alyksandr Sychou, police broke the arm of the Belarus diplomat, smashed his glasses and tore his clothes "despite the complete lack of resistance on their part."
Giuliani said seven witnesses support the police officers' account of the tiff with the diplomats. "They're certainly not going to get an apology," said Giuliani, a former federal prosecutor.
In fact, said Giuliani, Belarus should pay the city $41,400 for 828 outstanding summons issued to 15 vehicles in the first half of 1996.
"I expect that you will forward payment promptly," the mayor wrote in a letter to Belarus.
